Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: No evidence found for revenue collection via digital payments in CAR.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Fast-path check (single search) surfaced clearly authoritative evidence that CAR officially launched an e-Tax platform for online tax payment in March 2025, contradicting the original Unknown score; escalated to full path per routing rules. Both sources (Agence Ecofin and ITWeb Africa, an EU-backed government initiative) confirm the platform's télépaiement (e-payment) module. However customs revenue still runs through the separate ASYCUDA system (being upgraded to ASYCUDA World) and e-Tax rollout is still expanding beyond large taxpayers, so integration is partial rather than comprehensive. Revised from 0/Unknown to 2/Partial.
revised_comments: Central African Republic's Ministry of Finance and Budget officially launched the e-Tax platform on 24 March 2025, enabling registration, tax declaration and online tax payment for taxpayers, developed with European Union technical assistance. Customs revenue continues to be processed through the separate ASYCUDA customs system, which is being upgraded to ASYCUDA World, and e-Tax adoption is still expanding beyond initial large taxpayers. Digital payment integration with revenue collection is therefore partial rather than comprehensive.

revision_notes: Fast-path check found the e-Tax platform, which lets taxpayers pay taxes to government online — a direct P2G use case — contradicting the Unknown score; escalated to full path. revised_comments: Citizens and businesses in the Central African Republic can make person-to-government payments through the e-Tax platform launched in March 2025, which supports online tax declaration and payment. Uptake is still in an early phase: the government has run training workshops for tax agents and taxpayers and initially focused rollout on large taxpayers, so use of the system for P2G payments is limited rather than reflecting active, broad-based use.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: No evidence found for refugee/migrant access programs in CAR digital payments.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Fast-path check surfaced a directly relevant 2024 World Bank technical report on refugee economic inclusion in Central Africa, contradicting the Unknown score; escalated to full path. The report finds only around 5-7% of refugees in CAR hold the national ID typically required to open formal enterprise bank accounts, while a related report notes UNHCR proof-of-registration documentation allows refugees to open mobile money accounts in urban areas. This constitutes partial, documentation-dependent access rather than full or no access. Revised from 0/Unknown to 2/Partial.
revised_comments: Refugees and displaced persons in the Central African Republic can access mobile money accounts in urban areas using UNHCR proof-of-registration documentation, but only around 5-7% hold the national ID typically required to open formal enterprise bank accounts, and documentation and KYC requirements remain a barrier to fuller financial inclusion. Access to digital payment services for refugees and migrants is therefore partial rather than comprehensive or absent.
